callouts.title: Executive Overview
callouts.body: **Prompty** is a Microsoft-developed VS Code extension that standardizes LLM prompt development through a unified `.prompty` file format—combining prompt content, model configuration, and sample data in a single version-controlled asset. While designed primarily for [[OpenAI]] and [[Azure OpenAI]] workflows, it accelerates the "developer inner loop" of prompt engineering through rapid testing, preview capabilities, and code generation for production frameworks.

callouts.title: Critical Context for Your Setup
callouts.body: **Key Limitation:** Prompty does NOT natively integrate with [[Anthropic]] (Claude) or Google (Gemini) models. Your current setup uses [[Claude Code]] and [[Gemini Code Assist]], which are **separate tools** from Prompty. This reference note explains what Prompty does, its limitations, and strategic integration approaches for your multi-LLM prompt engineering library.

callouts.title: Prompty Asset Class
callouts.body: [**Prompty**:: a file format specification (`.prompty`) and VS Code extension designed to enhance observability, understandability, and portability for LLM prompt development by unifying prompt content, execution context, and sample data in a single version-controlled markdown asset.]^verified-stable

callouts.title: Accelerating the Developer Inner Loop
callouts.body: Prompty's primary goal is to reduce friction in the iterative prompt engineering cycle: write → test → observe → refine. By colocating all prompt components in a single file, developers avoid context switching between configuration files, test data, and prompt content.

callouts.title: Frontmatter Purpose
callouts.body: The frontmatter defines **who** (model configuration), **what** (input/output schemas), **how** (parameters), and **test data** (sample values) for the prompt execution.

callouts.title: Environment Variables Best Practice
callouts.body: Always use `${env:VAR_NAME}` syntax for API keys and endpoints. Store credentials in: - `.env` file in project root (add to `.gitignore`) - VS Code settings for team-shared configurations - System environment variables for global access

callouts.title: Multi-Modal Input Support
callouts.body: Prompty supports images and other media through Jinja2 template extensions, useful for vision-capable models like GPT-4o or Claude 3.5 Sonnet (if using proxy).

callouts.title: Prompty Extension Features
callouts.body: The VS Code extension provides an **interactive prompt playground** directly in your editor, eliminating the need to context-switch to web interfaces or external tools.

callouts.title: Configuration Strategy
callouts.body: For team collaboration: Use workspace-level `settings.json` with environment variable placeholders. For personal experimentation: Use user-level settings or inline configuration.

callouts.title: Iterative Prompt Engineering Cycle
callouts.body: Prompty optimizes the write → test → observe → refine cycle: 1. **Write** prompt in markdown with Jinja2 templates 2. **Test** with sample data via live preview 3. **Observe** output and verbose API trace 4. **Refine** prompt based on results 5. **Version** changes in Git 6. **Generate** production code when satisfied

callouts.title: Git Workflow Pattern
callouts.body:
```bash
# Create feature branch for prompt iteration
git checkout -b prompts/improve-customer-support

# Edit basic.prompty, test iterations
# Commit when satisfied with results
git add prompts/customer-support.prompty
git commit -m "Improve customer support prompt tone and structure"

# Push for team review
git push origin prompts/improve-customer-support
```

callouts.title: Framework Integration
callouts.body:
Right-click a `.prompty` file → select target framework → extension generates boilerplate code with:
- Prompt loading from file
- Variable injection
- Model configuration
- Response handling

callouts.title: Primary Limitation for Your Setup
callouts.body: **Prompty officially supports ONLY:** - [[OpenAI]] (direct API) - [[Azure OpenAI]] (Azure deployment) - **Serverless** (GitHub Marketplace models) **NOT supported:** - [[Anthropic]] (Claude models) - [[Google]] (Gemini models) - [[Cohere]], [[Mistral]], [[Groq]], etc.

callouts.title: Complexity Trade-Off
callouts.body: This approach adds infrastructure complexity and may not support all Prompty features (preview, tracing). Consider whether simpler approaches (direct API calls, alternative tools) better serve your workflow.

callouts.title: Hybrid Format Strategy
callouts.body: Adopt the `.prompty` format as your **standard prompt asset structure**, even for non-OpenAI prompts. Benefits: 1. **Version Control** — Git-friendly markdown format 2. **Discoverability** — All prompts follow same schema 3. **Documentation** — Frontmatter captures metadata 4. **Portability** — Easy migration if tooling improves 5. **PKB Integration** — Markdown files work natively in [[Obsidian]]

callouts.title: Modified .prompty for Non-OpenAI Providers
callouts.body:
Create a custom frontmatter field to document target provider:

```yaml
---
name: Code Review Assistant
provider: anthropic                    # Custom field
model_id: claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929  # Custom field
execution: manual                      # Custom field: manual | api | cli

model:
  api: chat
  configuration:
    # Leave as template - won't execute via Prompty
    type: openai_compatible
  parameters:
    max_tokens: 4000
    temperature: 0.3

sample:
  code: |
    def example():
        pass
---
# System
You are an expert code reviewer...
```

callouts.title: Markdown Compatibility
callouts.body: `.prompty` files are **pure markdown** with YAML frontmatter—exactly what [[Obsidian]] expects. They integrate seamlessly into your PKB as: - **Prompt library** — Searchable, version-controlled prompt collection - **Documentation** — Self-documenting with frontmatter metadata - **Templates** — Reusable prompt patterns - **Knowledge artifacts** — Linked to relevant PKB notes

callouts.title: Prompty Metadata as Dataview Fields
callouts.body:
Since Prompty uses YAML frontmatter, [[Dataview]] can query on:
- `name`, `description`, `version`, `tags`
- `model.api`, `model.configuration.type`
- `model.parameters.*`
- Any custom fields you add

callouts.title: Git + Obsidian + Prompty Workflow
callouts.body:
1. **Store** `.prompty` files in Obsidian vault (under version control)
2. **Open vault** in VS Code (where Obsidian and Prompty extensions coexist)
3. **Edit** prompts using Prompty features (OpenAI) or markdown (others)
4. **Commit** changes to Git
5. **Link** prompts from Obsidian notes using wiki-links
6. **Query** prompt library using Dataview

callouts.title: Prompty's Design Philosophy
callouts.body: Prompty embodies the principle that **prompts are code** and deserve the same engineering rigor: version control, testing, documentation, and reproducibility. By treating prompts as first-class assets rather than scattered strings, it enables: - **Collaboration** through standardized format - **Iteration** through rapid testing cycles - **Production** transition via code generation - **Observability** through request tracing

callouts.title: Prompt Engineering as Software Engineering
callouts.body:
The `.prompty` format parallels software engineering practices:
- **Specification** (frontmatter) = function signature + configuration
- **Implementation** (template) = function body
- **Sample data** = unit test fixtures
- **Execution** = function invocation
- **Version control** = Git workflow

callouts.title: When to Use Prompty
callouts.body: **Ideal for:** - [[OpenAI]] or [[Azure OpenAI]] prompt development - Team collaboration on prompt engineering - Production deployment via [[Prompt Flow]], [[LangChain]], [[Semantic Kernel]] - Rapid prototyping with sample data - Observable, traceable prompt iterations **Not ideal for:** - [[Anthropic]] (Claude) exclusive workflows (use [[Claude Code]] instead) - [[Google]] (Gemini) exclusive workflows (no native support) - Non-technical prompt iteration (web UIs may be simpler) - Already-established workflows with other prompt management tools

[MARKDOWN BODY: Prompt Template with Jinja2]

---
name: Basic Prompt                          # Descriptive identifier
description: A comprehensive prompt example  # Purpose documentation
version: 1.0.0                              # Semantic versioning
authors:                                     # Attribution
  - your-name
tags:                                        # Categorization
  - category
  - use-case

model:
  api: chat                                 # API type: chat | completion | embeddings
  configuration:
    type: azure_openai                      # Provider: azure_openai | openai | serverless
    azure_endpoint: ${env:AZURE_OPENAI_ENDPOINT}  # Environment variable syntax
    azure_deployment: gpt-4o                # Deployment/model name
    api_key: ${env:AZURE_OPENAI_API_KEY}   # API authentication
    api_version: 2024-10-21                 # API version
  parameters:
    max_tokens: 3000                        # Token limit
    temperature: 0.7                        # Randomness (0.0-2.0)
    top_p: 0.95                            # Nucleus sampling
    response_format: { "type": "json_object" }  # Optional: JSON mode

inputs:                                      # Input schema definition
  firstName:
    type: string
    description: User's first name
  question:
    type: string
    description: Question to answer

sample:                                      # Test data for preview/execution
  firstName: Jane
  lastName: Doe
  question: What is the meaning of life?
---
